issues.description: Method SealSaloon.checkOrderReady: the problem statement (UML and textual description) declares checkOrderReady() as returning void, but the solution implementation defines public boolean checkOrderReady(). This difference in return type (void vs boolean) is a structural API mismatch that will confuse students: the spec/UML instructs them to implement a void method while the reference solution and its callers use/expect a boolean return value.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return type consistent across artifacts. Preferably change the solution's method signature to match the problem statement: declare public void checkOrderReady() in SealSaloon and remove or adapt any boolean return/value logic inside (preserve behaviour of serving orders and printing). Alternatively, if the boolean return value is desired, update the problem statement UML and textual description to indicate checkOrderReady() returns boolean and document the meaning of the return value, and update any tests or examples accordingly.
